_meta.description: Source-trace for every shona phrase in lessons_consolidated.json. FSI = US State Department Shona Basic Course (1965), page references match the PDF in /archive/assets/.

mhoroi.context: used colloquially; FSI uses mangwanani/masikati but mhoro/mhoroi attested in cultural notes
mhoroi.note: attested in cultural_notes.json greetings section; treat as standard equivalent of mangwanani

shewe.english: sir / courteous address used by women

chirombowe.english: sir / courteous address used by men

kana mwaswerawo.english: if you also spent the day
kana mwaswerawo.context: unit 3 dialogue, courteous 'if you also' formula

baba vaswera senyi.english: how has your father spent the day?

vaswera zvavo zvirinane.english: he's better (he spent the day better)

vanhu.context: unit 5 implicit pl.; explicit in later units

munhu ndiani.english: who are you? (who is the person?)

Harare.context: unit 5 supplementary places — original FSI spells "Salisbury"; modern name is Harare

ku-.english: to / at (with place names and infinitive prefix)

gumi.english: ten (a noun, does not take concord)

tingaenda.english: we can go / may we go

anoita marinyi.english: how much is it? ('what money does it do?')

-ka-.english: past tense prefix (before today / general past)
-ka-.context: unit 13 note: vakaenda kwaMutare = they went to Umtali

unhu.english: humanness, ubuntu — 'i am because we are'

mhoro.note: modern equivalent to FSI mangwanani/masikati for informal contexts

-bereka.english: to carry (a child) on the back

-pera.english: to come to an end, be exhausted

gumi neposi.context: standard shona compound; FSI uses concord stems "gumi ne-mwe" for "eleven" implicitly through "gumi" + "ne-" + stem
gumi neposi.note: compound formed regularly from "gumi" (ten) + "ne-" (and) + counting form; the pattern is FSI-grounded but the literal phrase is the standard textbook formation

makumi maviri.context: standard plural pattern: "gumi" cl. 5 → plural "makumi" cl. 6; agreement "ma-viri" follows FSI unit 4 noun-class rules
makumi maviri.note: documented pattern: gumi pluralizes as makumi; "makumi maviri" follows the cl. 6 concord rule from FSI unit 4

mwabva kupi.note: natural sentence formed from FSI vocabulary

-rwara.english: to be sick (attested via "kurapa" = to heal)
-rwara.context: unit 5 verb list — implied by kurapa "to do medical work"
-rwara.note: core verb; widely attested in standard Shona

kare kare.context: standard storytelling opener; appears in many Shona folktales attested by Hannan and Fortune — cited in FSI bibliography
kare kare.note: common storytelling opener; documented in standard Shona literature

rimwe zuva.context: unit 41 tsuro naDiro: "Rimwe zuva, Tsuro naDiro vakapangana..."

kana mwararawo.context: parallel formation to "kana mwaswerawo" — unit 1 morning ritual
kana mwararawo.note: morning-greeting reciprocal; built on the same -wo pattern as kana mwaswerawo in unit 3

mwazviita.context: unit 14 dialogue: "Mwazvita, tambirayi" — thank you, here you are

handina kuenda.context: unit 13 past negative: handina kuenda navo

handina kuita.context: unit 13 past negative: handina kuita basa

simo.context: unit 14 basic dialogue: ndiri kutengesa masimo

-gadzira.context: unit 15: wagadzirireni? — what have you prepared?

pasi.english: down, on the ground, earth, floor

-chiri.context: unit 36 note: vachiri kufunda — they are still studying

wakange.context: unit 36 basic dialogue: iye wakange ari kutsvaka basa

-nga-form.context: unit 36 note: the /-nga-/ form fixes background time

gogogo.english: (knocking sound, said in lieu of knocking)

nhema.context: unit 38: yavo nhema iya — that black one

tose.english: all of us (the usual reply to makorokoto)

pachipamwe.english: (expression used on meeting someone already greeted that day)

-pumuza.english: to take a rest on a journey
-pumuza.context: unit 39: aiwa, tapumuza — "well, it's over with"

nzira.context: unit 16: iyi nzira ipfupi — this road is short
